items.title: Flipkart Tests Eat-In Food Delivery With 10% Commission For Restaurants
items.summary: Flipkart food delivery is entering the market to challenge Zomato and Swiggy. Can a lower commission model win over customers? Walmart India-backed Flipkart is preparing to disrupt the sector with its new service, Eat In by Minutes. By leveraging its existing logistics arm, Ekart, the company aims to challenge the duopoly of Zomato vs Swiggy. The strategy hinges on offering a 10 percent restaurant commission, significantly lower than the industry standard. Currently in testing with thousands of employees, this expansion into quick commerce is a direct attempt to capture market share. While Flipkart food delivery offers aggressive pricing, experts note that changing established consumer habits remains a major hurdle. items.title: How Lila Sciences’ AI and Automated Labs Help Scientists Discover New Medicines Faster
items.summary: Lila Sciences connects AI agents to an autonomous lab to explore a therapy designed to help a patient’s own immune cells fight B-cell lymphoma. In Lila’s AI Science Factory, robotic instruments make and test those candidates. The results return to inform the next round of designs and experiments. items.title: Claude Code + Spacesheep: How I Stay in the Loop
items.summary: Spacesheep is Claude Code artifacts on steroids: visual, interactive docs, plans and PR reviews, with comments and sharing. It's how I keep up with code that AI writes for me. This is my workflow with Claude Code and Spacesheep, start to finish, on a real feature for Semantic Router v1. We see what Spacesheep is and what people build with it. Then I plan the feature on a roadmap, have Claude Code (through Spacesheep) write a visual doc of the code I'm about to change, question the options with Spacesheep's built-in agent, and review the result on one page: a decision timeline, the API change, code notes and benchmarks. How I use Spacesheep: - Plan first: a roadmap linked to the issues in Linear, then a short plan for the feature. - Understand: ask for an interactive doc of the code, with the key snippets explained, and say why you want it so the agent can tailor it. - Discuss: question the agent's suggestions on the page itself, and choose between the options it lays out. - Review: a PR page with a timeline of every decision (which calls were mine), the code that changed, and what was measured. 🐑 Spacesheep: https://spacesheep.dev/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=creator&utm_campaign=james-briggs&utm_content=ss-1 The feature from this video, now merged and released in semantic-router v1.0.2: https://github.com/aurelio-labs/semantic-router/pull/778 ⏱️ Chapters 0:00 Keeping track of what AI builds 1:15 Visual docs 1:59 What people build with Spacesheep 2:24 How I use it: plan first 3:28 Today's build 4:14 What's there now 6:13 Is this the right option? 7:11 Following one query through the code 10:24 Picking a local model 11:31 Discuss the options 13:01 Spike first, then build 13:38 Review 14:57 The decision timeline 16:19 Measured on this branch 16:51 Stay in the loop 👋 Find me X: https://x.com/jamescalam LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamescalam/ GitHub: https://github.com/jamescalam #Spacesheep #ClaudeCode #ClaudeArtifacts

items.title: DeepSeek Just Open-Sourced How It Serves 155T Tokens a Day
items.summary: DeepSeek just open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its own API, along with a detailed write-up of how it serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at scale: 155 trillion tokens a day from a single cluster. In this video we follow one request through the system: deepseek-recipe tokenization and prompt-injection protection, a KV cache that DeepSeek keeps for days (96% of input tokens are cache hits), prefill and decode on different machines, expert parallelism across 64+ GPUs, DSpark speculative decoding, and batch-invariant inference. Then I test deepseek-recipe and the temperature-0 batching effect on my own Mac, and explain why DeepInfer won't run on a DGX Spark. DeepInfer (GitHub): https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer deepseek-recipe (GitHub): https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe DeepSeek's deployment write-up (Chinese): https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/2095560295930508953 English translation (Latent Space): https://x.com/latentspacepod/status/2112588380416647205 DeepSeek's announcement: https://x.com/deepseek_ai/status/2112476496283775135 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 weights: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 DeepSeek API pricing (cache hit vs miss): https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing Related videos: Speculative Decoding Explained: DeepSeek DSpark: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eFgknPFK-g0 Run a 284B Model in 128 GB (DwarfStar): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gHcmhUDJfw Chapters 00:00 DeepInfra 01:21 Prefill vs Decode Basics 03:07 Request Flow and Token Safety 04:31 KV Cache and Prefill Tricks 07:31 Decode at Scale MoE and Speculation 09:17 Batch Invariance and Real Limits 12:31 Hands On Tests and Key Takeaways

items.title: Self-Improving AI Could Arrive in One Year
items.summary: In episode 1037 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Richard Socher, CEO of Recursive how soon AI could start improving itself with no humans involved. Socher predicts that recursive self-improvement could arrive in less than two years, possibly in just one. He also warns that having RSI in the loop does not mean the strong takeoff scenario many people fear, and that a lot of those fears simply don't make sense.

items.summary: Introducing NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, an open hardware and software architecture for securing autonomous AI agents across the full stack. As agents take on long-running workflows at scale, safety requires controls outside the agents themselves. See why model alignment alone is not enough—and how models, tools, harnesses, and runtimes fit together. Without proper governance, agents can expose sensitive information, access unauthorized systems, or attempt to change their own permissions to complete a task. With models running on GPUs and harnesses and tools on CPUs, securing agents requires a systems approach. 📖 Read the press release → https://nvda.ws/4jzEjGv #NVIDIAGTC #AgenticAI #AISecurity #AISafety

items.title: How quantum computers are being used for drug discovery
items.summary: It can take more than a decade for a medical discovery to become a drug doctors can prescribe. You can read the full research here: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Researchers from @Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM are exploring how hybrid quantum-classical workflows could help accelerate this timeline–with exciting results. Earlier this year, the collaboration successfully simulated the chemistry of two protein complexes with binding agents, T4-Lysozyme and Trypsin. The largest simulation of a Trypsin complex reached 12,635 atoms and more than 30,000 orbitals, earning the milestone of largest heterogeneous quantum-classical (HQC) electronic-structure calculation to date: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Recently nominated as a 2026 Gordon Bell finalist (https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/gordon-bell-finalists-2026), the work showed an improvement in accuracy by 210x within a key step of the workflow over previous approaches, attained through new algorithm developments and the close integration of QPUs, CPUs and GPUs. In the latest entry of our research spotlight series, Dr. Kennie Merz. and Dr. Lara Jehi from Cleveland Clinic join IBM Quantum Head of Applied Quantum Science - Sarah Sheldon to explain how this deep integration of computing paradigms, known as quantum-centric supercomputing, helped achieve this remarkable moment in chemistry simulation at scale.

items.title: Amazon Launches Torch Neuron To Challenge Nvidia's Grip On PyTorch Developers
items.summary: AWS is challenging Nvidia dominance with the launch of Torch Neuron, a new tool designed to optimize AI performance and cost. Amazon Web Services has introduced this solution to allow PyTorch applications to run seamlessly on Trainium hardware. By shifting workloads to this custom infrastructure, AWS aims to provide a more cost-effective alternative for developers within the competitive AI software market, promising up to 70 percent more output per dollar spent. This move represents a strategic effort to lower the barrier to entry for large-scale model training.
